extName.message: Filtros MX — Ad blocker that catches the ads that slip through

extDescription.message: Blocks ads and trackers. If one slips through, it points it out and you remove it in one click. Free, open source, no telemetry.

notaApagado.message: Nothing is filtered on this site.

notaBasico.message: Only this site's own rules. Cleans less, but almost never breaks anything.

notaCompleto.message: Maximum cleanup. If something looks broken, try Basic.

notaExcluido.message: Filtros MX stays off here on purpose: it is a government services site with nothing to block.

bTitulo.message: Done. Filtros MX is already blocking.

bLema.message: Free, open source and no telemetry. Made in Mexico.

bFijarTitulo.message: One step: pin it to the toolbar

bFijar.message: Click the puzzle piece 🧩 at the top right of Chrome, then the pin next to Filtros MX. That way you see how much it removed on every page, and it is at hand if something slips through.

bHace1.message: Blocks ads and trackers right away, using EasyList, EasyPrivacy and EasyList Spanish — the open lists used by millions of people. Nothing to configure.

bHace2.message: Catches the ones that slip through. When an ad escapes every list, Filtros MX points it out in its icon and you remove it in one click.

bHace3.message: Removes whatever gets in your way. With “Remove an element” you pick anything on the page and it disappears — on future visits too.

bHaceYoutube.message: YouTube without video ads. Removes the ads before and during videos using the rules of uBlock Origin.

bHace4.message: You decide on every site. Full for maximum cleanup, Basic if a site acts up, Off if you want to support it.

bPriv1.message: Zero telemetry. Everything happens on your device: neither what you browse nor what gets blocked leaves your browser.

bPriv2.message: No paid “acceptable ads”. No advertiser can pay to get past the filter. Ever.

bPriv3.message: Truly free. No paid tier, no accounts, and the code is open for anyone to review.

bTodosTitulo.message: It has already improved the web for everyone

bTodos.message: The ads Filtros MX found on Mexican news sites were reported to EasyList Spanish: 12 reports, 11 already fully fixed. Today anyone using those lists blocks them, whatever blocker they use. If you find one, the extension drafts the report for you.

oCosmeticasAyuda.message: Closes the space the ad leaves behind. It is most of what the lists do: turning it off leaves almost everything without effect.

oGenericas.message: Full cleanup on every site · recommended

oGenericasAyuda.message: Also applies the general rules, which do not name any site. This is what cleans the most. If a site looks broken, set it to Basic from the icon. When off, every site starts in Basic.

oDetector.message: Tell me about ads that slip through

oDetectorAyuda.message: Looks on every page for ads no list covers. The analysis is local: nothing leaves your device.

oSitiosAyuda.message: What you set with the buttons in the icon, managed from here.

oSitiosVacio.message: None: every site uses the default mode.

oTuyasAyuda.message: What you removed with “Remove” or “Remove an element”. They are your own rules: they live on this device and are never sent anywhere.

oTuyasVacio.message: None yet. “Remove an element”, in the icon, creates the first one.

oFilaExtendidas.message: Advanced rules applied by our own engine

oFilaNoExt.message: Not applicable: advanced rules outside the engine

oComo1.message: Filtros MX blocks with the same public lists the most widely used blockers rely on — EasyList, EasyPrivacy and EasyList Spanish — maintained by hundreds of people. Your copy is from the date shown in the table above and is renewed with every version of the extension.

oComo2.message: On top of that, it catches the ads no list covers on the page you are viewing, lets you remove them in one click and, if you want, drafts the report so they get fixed for everyone.

oComo3.message: The table above also shows what could not be applied. A blocker that only shows off what made it in makes you believe you are better protected than you are.

oCredito.message: The base lists are by The EasyList authors, under GPLv3 and CC BY-SA 3.0. The YouTube rules and engine are by uBlock Origin (Raymond Hill and contributors), under GPLv3.
